input:
In this study, a gravity settler was employed for the removal of calcium carbonate from a process stream, and the sizing of the unit was carried out on the basis of a design overflow rate. The process stream enters the settler at a throughput of 357 m3 h-1, and with a design overflow rate of 2.1 m h-1, the required plan area of the settling zone works out at 170 m2.

The overflow rate can be understood as the throughput divided by the plan area, and it effectively represents the settling velocity that a particle must exceed if it is to be successfully removed rather than being carried out with the overflow stream. It should be noted that the overflow rate adopted here is based on a vendor rule for this particular solid, rather than on experimental settling data generated in the laboratory. Indeed, no settling test on the actual slurry has been carried out, which means that the sizing ultimately rests on the assumption that the vendor rule provides a reasonable representation of the settling behaviour of the calcium carbonate in this stream, an assumption that has not been independently verified.
target:
A gravity settler removes calcium carbonate from a process stream at a throughput of 357 m3 h-1. The settler is sized on a design overflow rate of 2.1 m h-1, and that rate gives a plan area of 170 m2 for the settling zone.

The overflow rate is the throughput divided by the plan area, and it has the dimensions of a velocity: it is the settling velocity a particle must exceed if it is to be removed. A particle that settles more slowly than the liquid rises towards the overflow leaves the settler with the overflow stream, so the overflow rate is the dividing value between the solids removed and the solids carried out. The plan area is the horizontal surface area of the settling zone, and once the throughput and the overflow rate are set, the area follows directly, with no other sizing variable left open.

The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the plan area holds only as far as the vendor rule represents the settling behaviour of the calcium carbonate in this stream. A slurry that settles more slowly than the rule assumes would pass solids to the overflow at this area, and would need a larger area at the same throughput.
